claim: “adjuncts relating to felicity conditions occur readily in questions, which modal adjuncts do not.”
evidence_summary: §16, p. 771: “Will he probably die? seems quite reasonable, and Won’t he probably die? is fully acceptable”, and examples with modal adjuncts like [11] “can readily be questioned”. Page 770 [12iib] Was he perhaps poisoned? is unmarked, with perhaps “likely to be construed as outside the scope of the question”. Ch. 3, p. 208: “The subjectivity of perhaps is reflected in its occurrence in interrogatives outside the scope of the question”.
finding: Medium confidence. The defence that p. 775 means modal adjuncts seldom fall inside a question’s scope (p. 770, “modality is more readily questioned by a predication than a modification construction”) partly works. But the felicity adjuncts of [5ii–iii] are outside the question’s scope too, and p. 771 still says such examples “can readily be questioned”.
inference: Do modal adjuncts occur readily in questions?

evidence.passage: §18, p. 775. “adjuncts relating to felicity conditions occur readily in questions, which modal adjuncts do not”
evidence.example: Page 771, Will he probably die? Page 770 [12iib] Was he perhaps poisoned? Ch. 3, p. 208, Has he perhaps missed his train?
evidence.establishes: §16 and Ch. 3 give modal adjuncts in questions as acceptable.
